problem_type: Credential-bearing outbound requests followed redirects without constraining the next origin
symptom: A local two-port HTTP fixture showed a 302/307/308 response forwarding custom authentication headers to the second port; 307/308 also replayed the POST body.
direct_cause: appFetch (the sole Node HTTP entry) passed the caller's options straight to native fetch, whose default is to follow redirects. The outbound guard checked only the initial URL, and a per-caller redirect option existed on only a few call sites.
class_root: The transport boundary had no rule for credential-bearing requests: whether a redirect was followed depended on each caller remembering to set an option, so every new credentialed caller (and every caller written before the rule) was open.
affected_population: Any vendor generation, upload, audio or probe request carrying an API key, tenant key, authorization header, custom gateway header, or POST body
Users testing a custom onboarding endpoint whose first response is a cross-origin redirect
Any 302, 307, or 308 response produced by a provider, relay, proxy, captive portal, or misconfigured endpoint
Users whose provider address legitimately redirects (http to https, trailing slash, regional domain): they now get a clear failure instead of a silent follow
internal_only_reason: The invariant is an application transport rule enforced at Nomi's request boundaries; the audited behavior is determined by the native fetch contract and this repository's credential ownership, not by a provider API specification.

invariant_owner_layer.rationale: The rule is judged once, in withCredentialRedirectPolicy, and applied by the sole outbound entry appFetch. The test drives the real appFetch (the global test setup swaps it for a pass-through, so the file unmocks it) against local two-port 302/307/308 servers through four doors and asserts the second port receives nothing.

invariants: A request carrying any header outside the plain set never auto-follows a redirect
A redirect response cannot cause a second-origin request containing authorization, x-api-key, a relay-specific auth header, cookie, or a sensitive POST body
A caller that sets redirect itself (hardenedFetch hop-by-hop header stripping, model-list manual pagination, direct key probe) keeps its own validated handling
Plain requests without credentials (asset downloads) still follow redirects
A refused redirect is reported in the user's language with the next step, never as a bare fetch failure

door_reduction.why_not: The 24 appFetch doors (16 write, 8 read; node scripts/door-map.mjs appFetch) were collapsed into the one place they all pass through: the redirect rule is derived inside appFetch from the request's own headers instead of being set per call site. The other five doors listed are not second copies of the rule: they are the three places that turn the refusal into the user-facing sentence (generation requests, onboarding probes, audio upload; each already had its own failure formatter) plus the helper that recognises it and the predicate that judges credentials. Per-site redirect options added earlier in this branch were removed.

generality_proof: node scripts/door-map.mjs appFetch listed every outbound entry: vendor transport, onboarding probes, AI SDK profiled fetch, multipart and audio upload, image-edit and native endpoint probes, local asset download, ComfyUI helpers, telemetry. All pass through appFetch, so the rule applies to each regardless of caller, provider or version. The remaining non-appFetch senders were scanned (net.fetch, https.request, undici, direct fetch): hardenedFetch and fetchModelList handle redirects manually with their own origin checks, directKeyCredential and the MCP loopback request already send redirect:error, and the browser-media fetch carries only Accept and Referer.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Decides once whether a request carries credentials and, if so, sets native redirect:error unless the caller chose its own redirect handling.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Reaches appFetch through fetchVendorWithBaseFallback; authored headers make the request credentialed, and a refused redirect is mapped to the credential-redirect code (non-retryable).
First send and official-fallback resend both go through appFetch; no per-site option remains.
Unauthenticated GET used only to identify an official candidate; carries no credential.
POST with auth headers goes through appFetch; the refusal is shown with the desktop string network.credentialRedirect.

Sets redirect:manual itself and validates every pagination link; the policy respects an explicit redirect. A 3xx now fails with the redirect failure kind and a sentence naming the target host and path.
AI SDK requests carry provider headers and go through appFetch; the policy applies without a per-caller option.
Reference-media upload senders go through requestVendor or appFetch with auth headers; same policy.
Authorization POST goes through appFetch; a refused redirect is reported with the same user-facing sentence.
Already sends redirect:error explicitly; the policy leaves an explicit choice alone.
Sets redirect:manual and strips credential headers on a cross-origin hop itself; explicit choice respected.
Carries only Accept and Referer, no Nomi credential.
The pass-through double applies withCredentialRedirectPolicy, so domain tests do not run under a looser rule than production.

recurrence.reason: Redirect handling is transport behavior. Any provider, relay, captive portal, proxy, or future caller can return a redirect, and custom headers/body replay is independent of provider identity.
same_class_scan: scan electron for net.fetch, https.request, undici request and direct fetch (none carry Nomi credentials outside the list above)

prevention.invariant: Every request that goes through appFetch and carries a header outside the plain set is sent with redirect:error unless the caller chose another redirect mode.
prevention.failure_mode: Native fetch rejects the redirect before a second-origin request is made; vendor and onboarding callers report it in the user's language and tell the user to change the provider address to the redirect target.
prevention.strategy: Derive the rule from the request at the earliest shared boundary instead of setting an option at call sites; fail closed on unknown headers because vendors choose their own auth header names. The native redirect option is the whole mechanism; a caller that already sets redirect itself (hardenedFetch hop-by-hop header stripping, model-list manual pagination) is not overridden because it validates each hop on its own.

legacy_paths.rationale: Per-call-site redirect options existed only in the first revision of this branch and never reached main; the final change has a single rule in credentialRedirectPolicy.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency upgrade is needed. The fix binds the application invariant through RequestInit and existing native fetch behavior.

migration: No persisted data or external contract changes. Providers that redirect now fail with an actionable message instead of being followed; users change the provider address to the redirect target.
residual_risks: Outside the model-list fetch (which uses manual mode and can read Location), the refusal does not name the redirect target: native fetch reports only that a redirect happened, so the message asks the user to look up the final address.
A request whose only secret is in the URL query or body, with no header outside the plain set, is not treated as credentialed.
Live providers, paid requests and domestic no-proxy networking were not exercised.
